title: Mycolic acid as a Wikipedia lipid class
dek: α-alkyl β-hydroxy long-chain fatty acids. Encyclopedia lipid node. FAS-II/InhA chemistry stays on tb-mycolates and tb-isoniazid.
story: Mycolic acids on Wikipedia are a lipid class: very long α-branched, β-hydroxy fatty acids that define the mycobacterial (and related) outer envelope. The page will mention C60–C90 in Mtb and acid-fastness as a consequence.
Simplfy already has a mycolate biosynthesis plate and INH/ETH targeting InhA. This card is the dictionary class those pathways assemble.
Corynebacteria and Nocardia make shorter mycolates. That is why acid-fastness is a family resemblance, not a TB barcode.
deep: TDM (cord factor) is a mycolate glycoconjugate — neighbouring plate.
Covalent attachment to arabinogalactan is the envelope sandwich (tb-cell-envelope).
Do not take INH doses from a lipid page.
Mass-spec mycolate profiling is research/ID niche, not a WRD.

visual.caption: Lipid class sitting in the envelope stack. Drug names are pointers, not doses.
